units.name: Las cinco vocales
lesson: Spanish has only five vowel sounds, and each one always sounds the same. Keep them short and clean, with no glide at the end.
For a French speaker: a as in patte, e between é and è, i as in ici, o as in mot, u as in ou.
Every vowel is pronounced, even at the end of a word: mesa is me-sa, never mez.

items.tip: A-gua: the u slides into the a, like ou-a
eu-RO-pa: hear both e and u

units.name: Letras que cambian
lesson: h is always silent: hola sounds like ola.
j, and g before e or i, is a rough sound from the back of the throat, like a strong h or the ch in Bach.
ll and y sound like the y in yes. ñ is the gn of montagne.
qu sounds like k, and gu before e or i is a hard g. The u is silent.
c before e or i, and z: in Spain it's the th of English think; in Latin America it's an s.

items.tip: YE-lo: h silent, hie sounds like ye
HEN-te: g before e is throaty

units.name: La r y la rr
units.english: The tapped r and rolled rr
lesson: A single r between vowels is one quick tap of the tongue tip, like the tt in American 'butter'.
rr, and an r at the start of a word, is rolled: several fast taps.
Keep the r at the front of the mouth. The French throat r is the most common trap for French speakers.
Changing r to rr changes the word: pero means but, perro means dog.

items.tip: RRÁ-pi-do: an r at the start is rolled
one tap right after the t
co-RRER: rolled, then a tap at the end
do-LOR: light tongue tap at the end, not a French r

units.name: b, v y la d suave
units.english: b, v and the soft d
lesson: b and v are the same sound in Spanish. Never use the French v.
At the start of a phrase or after m or n, it's a full b. Between vowels it softens: the lips almost touch.
d between vowels or at the end of a word is soft, close to the th in English 'the'. At the very end it almost disappears.

items.tip: first b full, second b soft
sa-LUD: the final d nearly disappears

units.name: El acento tónico
lesson: Words ending in a vowel, n or s are stressed on the second-to-last syllable: CA-sa, HA-blan.
Words ending in any other consonant are stressed on the last syllable: hos-pi-TAL, do-LOR.
A written accent breaks the rule and shows where the stress goes: MÚS-cu-lo, a-QUÍ.
French always stresses the end of the word. Spanish stress moves, and putting it in the wrong place can make a word hard to understand.

items.tip: os-pi-TAL: ends in l, so stress at the end

units.name: Saludos y cortesía
lesson: Use usted with patients and people you don't know. It works like vous. Use tú with friends and family, like tu.
With usted, the verb takes the same form as for él / ella: ¿Cómo está usted?
Buenos días until about noon, buenas tardes until dark, buenas noches in the evening.

units.name: Presentarse
lesson: Me llamo literally means I call myself. Soy comes from ser, used for who you are and your job.
Learn the survival phrases early. They keep a conversation going when you get lost.

items.tip: y (and) becomes e before a word starting with i

items.english: How do you say … in Spanish?

units.name: Números y días
lesson: 1 to 10: uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez.
Days take el and no capital letter: el lunes = on Monday, los lunes = on Mondays.
You'll use numbers all day in the clinic: pain scores, repetitions, times.

units.name: Verbos esenciales
lesson: Ser is for what something is: identity, job, origin (Soy fisioterapeuta). Estar is for states and places (Estoy cansado, Estoy en la clínica). French uses être for both.
Doler works like plaire: the thing that hurts is the subject. Me duele la rodilla (one thing), me duelen las rodillas (several).
Each card shows the infinitive. The tip gives the two forms you'll need most: yo and usted.

units.name: Preguntas
lesson: Questions open with ¿ and close with ?. Question words always carry a written accent.
For a yes/no question, keep the sentence and raise your voice at the end: ¿Le duele?

units.name: El cuerpo
lesson: Learn each body part with its article. The gender doesn't always match French: el hombro but l'épaule.
Spanish says me duele la mano (the hand hurts me), using the article, not mi.

units.name: Síntomas
lesson: Tengo dolor de … is the neutral way to describe pain. Me duele … is more everyday.
Siento + noun describes sensations: Siento hormigueo en la mano.

units.name: Movimientos
lesson: These verbs are the core of every exercise instruction. Learn the infinitive here; Level 4 turns them into commands for patients.
Reflexive verbs end in -se: sentarse (to sit down), acostarse (to lie down), like s'asseoir.

units.name: Contar lo que pasó
lesson: Patients describe injuries in the past tense (pretérito): Me caí, me torcí el tobillo.
Hace + time means ago: hace dos semanas = il y a deux semaines.
Focus first on understanding these forms. Saying them comes later.

items.french: Je me suis tordu la cheville.
Ça a commencé il y a deux semaines.
Je me suis réveillé avec de la douleur.

units.name: Recepción
lesson: At reception everything uses usted. Siéntese and pase are commands for usted.
Times: a las tres y media (3:30), a las diez y cuarto (10:15).

items.french: Quelle est votre date de naissance ?
Remplissez ce formulaire, s'il vous plaît.
Je suis à vous dans un instant.

items.spanish: Su próxima cita es el martes.
items.english: Your next appointment is on Tuesday.

units.name: La entrevista
lesson: These questions follow the order of a normal subjective exam. Learn them as whole phrases.
le means to you (formal): ¿Le duele? = does it hurt you, ¿Qué le pasó? = what happened to you.

items.spanish: Del cero al diez, ¿cuánto le duele?
items.english: From 0 to 10, how much does it hurt?
items.french: De zéro à dix, à quel point avez-vous mal ?

items.english: Does the pain go down your leg?
items.french: La douleur descend-elle dans la jambe ?

items.english: What do you do for work?

units.name: Instrucciones del examen
lesson: Commands for usted end in -e for -ar verbs (levante, doble) and -a for -er and -ir verbs (haga, mantenga).
With reflexive verbs the pronoun attaches to the end: siéntese, acuéstese, relájese. That's why they carry an accent.

units.name: Ejercicios en casa
lesson: Haga (do) and mantenga (hold) come from hacer and mantener. Pare (stop) comes from parar.
Series = sets, repeticiones = reps, veces = times: dos veces al día.
examples: Haga tres series de diez repeticiones.

items.spanish: Haga tres series de diez repeticiones.
items.english: Do three sets of ten repetitions.
items.french: Faites trois séries de dix répétitions.

items.english: Hold the position for ten seconds.
Put ice on for fifteen minutes.
items.french: Mettez de la glace quinze minutes.

units.name: Anatomía clínica
lesson: Most anatomy terms come from Latin, so they're close to French. The traps are the stress and the gender.
Plurals matter: los isquiotibiales (the hamstrings), los glúteos.

units.name: Diagnósticos
lesson: Many diagnoses end in -itis (inflammation) or -algia (pain), as in French.
Patients often use everyday names: codo de tenista instead of epicondilitis, hombro congelado instead of capsulitis adhesiva.

units.name: Evaluación
lesson: Voy a + infinitive (I'm going to …) lets you announce each step of the exam, which reassures the patient.
Ask patients to compare sides: el lado derecho, el lado izquierdo.
examples: ¿Siente lo mismo en los dos lados?

items.english: I'm going to assess your shoulder.
I'm going to palpate the area.

items.spanish: ¿Siente lo mismo en los dos lados?
items.english: Do you feel the same on both sides?
items.french: Sentez-vous la même chose des deux côtés ?

units.name: Tratamiento
lesson: Voy a also works for treatment: Voy a hacer una movilización.
Dar de alta means to discharge a patient: Le doy de alta.

units.name: Vestibular
lesson: Patients rarely use vértigo precisely. Ask whether things spin (da vueltas) or whether they feel unsteady (inestable).
Al + infinitive means when doing something: al girarse en la cama = when turning over in bed.
examples: Mantenga los ojos abiertos y mire mi nariz.

items.english: Do you feel like everything is spinning?

items.spanish: ¿El mareo aparece al girarse en la cama?
items.english: Does the dizziness come on when you turn over in bed?
items.french: L'étourdissement apparaît-il quand vous vous tournez dans le lit ?

items.english: How long does the dizziness last?

items.spanish: Voy a mover su cabeza rápidamente.
items.english: I'm going to move your head quickly.
items.french: Je vais bouger votre tête rapidement.

items.spanish: Mantenga los ojos abiertos y mire mi nariz.
items.english: Keep your eyes open and look at my nose.
items.french: Gardez les yeux ouverts et regardez mon nez.

items.spanish: Es normal sentir mareo durante la maniobra.
items.english: It's normal to feel dizzy during the maneuver.
items.french: Il est normal d'être étourdi pendant la manœuvre.

units.name: Explicar y educar
lesson: After Es importante que, Le recomiendo que and El objetivo es que, Spanish uses the subjunctive, like French il faut que: que siga, que haga, que vuelva.
Short, calm sentences work best for pain education. Learn these as models and adapt them.
examples: El dolor no siempre significa daño.

items.spanish: El dolor no siempre significa daño.
items.french: La douleur ne signifie pas toujours une lésion.

items.spanish: Es normal sentir un poco de molestia.
items.english: It's normal to feel a little discomfort.
items.french: Il est normal de ressentir un peu d'inconfort.

items.english: It's important that you keep moving.
items.french: Il est important que vous continuiez à bouger.

items.spanish: Le recomiendo que haga los ejercicios cada día.
items.english: I recommend you do the exercises every day.
items.french: Je vous recommande de faire les exercices chaque jour.

items.spanish: Hay que fortalecer los músculos de la cadera.
items.french: Il faut renforcer les muscles de la hanche.

items.spanish: La recuperación suele tardar de seis a ocho semanas.
items.english: Recovery usually takes six to eight weeks.
items.french: La récupération prend habituellement de six à huit semaines.

items.spanish: El objetivo es que vuelva a correr sin dolor.
items.english: The goal is for you to run again without pain.
items.french: L'objectif est que vous puissiez recourir sans douleur.

items.spanish: Su cuerpo se adapta poco a poco.
items.english: Your body adapts little by little.
items.french: Votre corps s'adapte petit à petit.

items.english: We're going to improve your mobility.

items.spanish: Si el dolor aumenta, reduzca la intensidad.
items.english: If the pain increases, reduce the intensity.
items.french: Si la douleur augmente, réduisez l'intensité.

units.name: La conversación clínica
lesson: Ask before touching: ¿Me da permiso para …? is polite and clear.
Según (according to) and parece que (it seems that) let you share findings without sounding absolute.
examples: ¿Me da permiso para tocarle el hombro?

items.spanish: ¿Me da permiso para tocarle el hombro?
items.french: Me permettez-vous de toucher votre épaule ?

items.spanish: Según la evaluación, parece que es muscular.
items.english: From the assessment, it seems to be muscular.
items.french: Selon l'évaluation, il semble que ce soit musculaire.

items.spanish: ¿Está de acuerdo con el plan de tratamiento?
items.english: Do you agree with the treatment plan?
items.french: Êtes-vous d'accord avec le plan de traitement ?

items.spanish: Si nota hormigueo o pérdida de fuerza, avíseme enseguida.
items.english: If you notice tingling or loss of strength, tell me right away.
items.french: Si vous remarquez des fourmillements ou une perte de force, avisez-moi tout de suite.

items.spanish: Le voy a derivar a su médico.
items.english: I'm going to refer you to your doctor.
items.french: Je vais vous diriger vers votre médecin.

items.spanish: Le haré un informe para su médico.
items.english: I'll write a report for your doctor.
items.french: Je vais faire un rapport pour votre médecin.

items.spanish: ¿Cómo le fue la semana con los ejercicios?
items.english: How did the week go with the exercises?
items.french: Comment s'est passée la semaine avec les exercices ?
Vous vous êtes beaucoup amélioré, félicitations !

items.english: We're going to adjust the program.
